Partial correlations from a joint graphical lasso fit

Source: R/methods-jgl.R
pcor_estimate.jgl.Rd

pcor_estimate() method for fits from JGL::JGL() (class "jgl"; Danaher, Wang & Witten 2014): converts each group's estimated precision matrix with precision_to_pcor(). It only reads fit$theta, so ggmtools does not depend on JGL. (JGL was archived on CRAN in July 2025; it can be installed from the CRAN archive or with remotes::install_github("cran/JGL").)

Usage

# S3 method for class 'jgl'
pcor_estimate(fit, varnames = NULL, groupnames = NULL, ...)

Arguments

fit

A "jgl" object from JGL::JGL(), fitted with return.whole.theta = TRUE. With the default return.whole.theta = FALSE, JGL drops variables that are not connected to any other, and the method stops with an error.

varnames

Optional variable names. Defaults to the dimnames of the estimates (JGL keeps the column names of the data), then V1, ..., Vp.

groupnames

Optional group names. JGL does not store them, so they default to Group_1, ..., Group_K; pass names(data_list) to use the names of the data list.

...

Ignored.

Value

A named list of K symmetric p x p partial-correlation matrices, as described in pcor_estimate(). These are penalized point estimates: entries the penalty sets to zero are exactly 0.

References

Danaher, P., Wang, P. & Witten, D.M. (2014). The joint graphical lasso for inverse covariance estimation across multiple classes. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 76(2), 373-397.

See also

ggm_bic() for tuning the penalties.

Examples

# A minimal object with the structure JGL::JGL() returns
theta <- list(diag(3), matrix(c(2, -0.5, 0, -0.5, 2, 0, 0, 0, 1), 3, 3))
fit <- structure(list(theta = theta, connected = rep(TRUE, 3)), class = "jgl")
pcor_estimate(fit, varnames = c("a", "b", "c"), groupnames = c("A", "B"))
#> $A
#>   a b c
#> a 1 0 0
#> b 0 1 0
#> c 0 0 1
#> 
#> $B
#>      a    b c
#> a 1.00 0.25 0
#> b 0.25 1.00 0
#> c 0.00 0.00 1
#>
